findings.body:
**Handle marker-persistence failures as acquired admission.**

In `deploy-runbook.py`, Line 368 creates `runner-disabled` before this assignment. If writing, flushing or fsyncing the token fails, the marker remains but `acquired` stays `False`. `restore_before_switch` then returns at Line 1043. The command reports an unchanged-host refusal with exit 2, although admission remains disabled.

Track successful marker creation separately from successful token persistence. Remove the marker only when ownership is proven. Otherwise, report recovery required with the retained marker identity.
findings.title: Handle marker-persistence failures as acquired admission.

findings.body:
**Keep health failures inside the JSON error path.**

In `deploy-controller.py`, Line 2222 rethrows health errors. If receipt-directory enumeration raises `OSError`, Line 2238 raises `SystemExit(str(exc))`. This leaves stdout empty and writes the error to stderr, including under `--json`. Python documents this string-exit behavior. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.10/library/sys.html))

Emit one error artifact and return exit 1 instead. Keep narration conditional on machine mode.

As per coding guidelines, I1 requires “stdout is JSON” and “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty.”
findings.title: Keep health failures inside the JSON error path.

findings.body:
**Capture systemctl stderr in machine mode.**

In `deploy-runbook.py`, Line 313 leaves child stderr inherited. The separate `check_output` call at Line 326 does the same. If `systemctl` reports a bus or start failure, its diagnostic reaches stderr even under `--json`. Suppressing `Run.narrate` cannot suppress child output. Python documents this inheritance behavior. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.10/library/subprocess.html))

Capture stderr in both calls. Carry the diagnostic into the JSON error or conditional narration.

As per coding guidelines, I1 requires “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty.”
findings.title: Capture systemctl stderr in machine mode.

findings.body:
**Run the controller's unfinished-transaction guard before the checkout switch.**

`deploy-runbook.py:604` binds `Effects` to `self.run_dir`, a per-run directory. The controller's `refuse_unfinished_transactions` checks the controller's record directory, so this runbook never inspects the records that matter here. The runbook also never calls `refuse_unfinished_transactions`. The controller's `deploy_plan` calls it before the checkout switch, and the runbook bypasses `deploy_plan`. A pre-activation or unfinished checkout or unit-switch record in the controller record directory is therefore not seen. The runbook can change the checkout while that transaction still needs recovery.

Before `helper.switch`, call `refuse_unfinished_transactions` on an `Effects` bound to the controller record directory that `deploy-controller.py` uses. Refuse the deployment when that check finds any unfinished record.
findings.title: Run the controller's unfinished-transaction guard before the checkout switch.

findings.body:
**Serialize runbook deploys with controller transactions.**

`deploy-runbook.py` serializes only against other runbook runs. It takes `state/deploy.lock` at line 586 and switches the checkout at lines 654 and 951. Controller transactions take `controller.lock` through `controller_lock()` at `deploy-controller.py:325-343`, at its call sites on lines 1397, 1466, 1813, and 1997. Neither side takes the other's lock.

The runbook claims admission with `state/runner-disabled`, but no controller or binding code reads that marker or `deploy.lock`. A controller `--unit` switch can therefore start during the runbook's checkout switch or released health window. The runbook's digest checks can detect some changes after they happen, but they do not prevent the overlap.

Put both entrypoints behind one shared exclusion before any mutation. Either the runbook acquires `controller.lock` through `self.effects.controller_lock()`, or the controller transactions refuse while `deploy.lock` is held. The change needs a shared lock path, so no single-line patch is safe here.
findings.title: Serialize runbook deploys with controller transactions.
